title: Area between two Curves

## Area between two Curves

### Problem
If $m$ is a positive real number and the area enclosed by the graphs of $y = mx$ and $y = x^2$ is 9, determine the value of $m$.

### Solution (adapted from the official solution)
The value of $m$ is $\sqrt[3]{54} = 3\sqrt[3]{2}$.

The intersection points of $y = mx$ and $y = x^2$ satisfy $x^2 = mx \implies x(x - m) = 0$, giving $x = 0$ and $x = m$.
On the interval $[0, m]$, the line $y = mx$ lies above the parabola $y = x^2$.

The enclosed area is:

$$\int_0^m (mx - x^2) \, dx = \left[ \frac{mx^2}{2} - \frac{x^3}{3} \right]_0^m = \frac{m^3}{2} - \frac{m^3}{3} = \frac{m^3}{6}.$$

Setting this equal to 9:

$$\frac{m^3}{6} = 9 \implies m^3 = 54 \implies m = \sqrt[3]{54} = 3\sqrt[3]{2}.$$

### Conceptual Explanation
Integrating $mx - x^2$ from $0$ to $m$ gives $\frac{m^3}{6}$. Equating this to 9 yields $m^3 = 54$, so $m = 3\sqrt[3]{2}$.

### Key Technique
Integration of vertical difference between line and parabola $\int_0^m (mx - x^2) dx = m^3/6$.
